key_battle: QB Efficiency: NO has the clearest edge over NYG — score 5.7/10.

football_factors.name: QB Efficiency
football_factors.reason: NO's QB efficiency is modestly higher than NYG's this season (0.144 EPA/play difference) — a gap that shapes drive consistency and big-play rate.

football_factors.name: Turnover Edge
football_factors.reason: NYG wins the turnover battle modestly — a 0.60 turnover-per-game edge that creates shorter fields and extra possessions.

football_factors.name: Offensive Efficiency
football_factors.reason: NO's offense generates slightly more expected points per play than NYG's (0.026 EPA/play difference), keeping drives alive and converting more consistently.

football_factors.name: Defensive Resistance
football_factors.reason: NO's defense is slightly more stingy than NYG's — allowing 0.015 fewer EPA per play and limiting opponent scoring opportunities.

football_factors.name: Pressure Matchup
football_factors.reason: NO wins the pass rush vs. protection battle slightly (0.006 sack-rate edge) — a mismatch that can collapse key third-down drives.

explanation: Clark leans NYG at 57%. NYG hold a +0.03 EPA/play edge over NO across the last three games. The main risk is plain variance — a turnover or a special-teams swing can compress the edge fast.
market_note: The market also favors NYG via a 2.5-point spread, aligning with the model. Football factors — QB Efficiency and Turnover Edge — are the primary driver, with market data providing secondary confirmation.

game_diagnosis.headline: Slight lean: NYG at 57.0%
game_diagnosis.football_story: Clark leans NYG at 57%. NYG hold a +0.03 EPA/play edge over NO across the last three games. The main risk is plain variance — a turnover or a special-teams swing can compress the edge fast.
game_diagnosis.primary_reason: Rest, venue, and weather all come out close to even here, so this factor barely moves the needle.
game_diagnosis.secondary_reason: Neither defense has clearly separated on a per-play basis lately — NYG allow -0.13 EPA/play more than NO recently, essentially a wash. The model gives NYG a slight edge in the overall blend rather than in any one number. If they keep NO uncomfortable, NO's scoring drives are the ones that stall out.
game_diagnosis.risk_factor: The main risk is game-state variance: a turnover, a special-teams breakdown, or an early injury can compress the statistical edge quickly.
flip_scenarios: If NYG loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.
If NO converts its EPA edge into red-zone touchdowns, the model's lean can flip.

factor_cards.headline: The setting is close to neutral.
factor_cards.explanation: Rest, venue, and weather all come out close to even here, so this factor barely moves the needle.
factor_cards.baseline_note: NO 0d rest

factor_cards.name: Defensive Edge
factor_cards.headline: NYG grade out as the slightly better defense.

factor_cards.name: Recent Offense
factor_cards.headline: NYG's offense is heating up.

factor_cards.baseline_note: NYG hold a +0.03 EPA/play edge over NO across the last three games.

factor_cards.name: Momentum
factor_cards.headline: Recent form is close to even.

factor_cards.baseline_note: Recent form grades out close between NYG and NO.

factor_cards.name: Market Edge
factor_cards.headline: Vegas gives Even the slight nod.
factor_cards.explanation: Here Clark is taking the other side of the market — Vegas actually made NYG a 2.5-point favorite — about a 45% implied win probability. That disagreement is the interesting part: the model sees something in the football matchup the line is underrating.
factor_cards.baseline_note: Market line: NYG a 2.5-point favorite.
